v.why: Raising an already high learning rate causes divergence and large accuracy drops.
At tiny learning rates training is underfit within 243 epochs, so increasing LR helps.
Lowering a divergent high learning rate recovers large amounts of accuracy.
Strong L2 penalties push the model into underfitting, so increasing alpha further hurts much more than at negligible alpha.
Reducing an over-regularizing alpha restores capacity and accuracy.
Very small batches give noisy, unstable updates, so enlarging them helps more than at larger batch sizes.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at high learning rates.
Deeper networks are more prone to divergence at high learning rates.
At low learning rates, extra depth adds useful capacity without instability.
Wider layers with a high learning rate tend to destabilize training, so widening hurts there.

raw:
Ten hypotheses, each grounded in the experiments:

1. **Learning rate up is worse at high LR.** When the learning rate is already in the high band (≥0.0774), raising it again causes large drops (#13, #14, #16, #17).
2. **Learning rate up is better at low LR.** When the learning rate is in the low band, raising it helps (#12, #15).
3. **Learning rate down is better at high LR.** Lowering a high learning rate gives large gains (#21–#24).
4. **Alpha up is worse at high alpha.** When alpha is already high (≥0.129), raising it hurts more (#77, #80–#87 vs. #78, #93).
5. **Alpha down is better at high alpha.** Lowering a high alpha recovers several points of accuracy (#96–#100).
6. **Batch size up is better at small batch.** Larger batches help most when the batch is very small, especially with high alpha or high LR (#31, #40, #43).
7. **Batch size up is better at high LR.** At a high learning rate, a bigger batch stabilizes training (#30, #40).
8. **Depth up is worse at high LR.** Adding depth at a high learning rate is catastrophic (#66, #67).
9. **Depth up is better at low LR.** At a low learning rate, extra depth helps more (#65, #74).
10. **Width up is worse at high LR.** Wider networks at a high learning rate tend to diverge (#50, #57).
